title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: share a chat session or a single response by link
summary: Pass: Microsoft's documentation and tenant notice support the default-on sharing behaviour, tenant-wide switch, administrator roles and rollout details. Minor corrections concern the product's current name and checklist controls that are missing from the controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot users can share chat content through a link.
claims.quote: Session and Response Sharing let Microsoft 365 Copilot users share Copilot chat content through a link.

claims.claim: Session sharing includes the entire conversation's prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Session sharing lets users share an entire Copilot conversation, including all prompts and responses.

claims.claim: Response sharing includes one response and the prompt that generated it.
claims.quote: Response sharing lets users share a single Copilot response along with the prompt that generated it.

claims.claim: Shared content opens in a read-only view.
claims.quote: The shared content opens as a read-only view, and recipients can continue from it in their own Copilot chat.

claims.claim: Recipients can continue from shared content in their own Copilot chat.
claims.quote: The shared content opens as a read-only view, and recipients can continue from it in their own Copilot chat.

claims.claim: Shared content is a snapshot of the content at sharing time.
claims.quote: Shared conversations and responses are snapshots. People who open your link can't change your original conversation.

claims.claim: Continuing from shared content creates a separate copy in the recipient's chat history.
claims.quote: If they continue from shared content, Copilot creates a separate copy in their own chat history.

claims.claim: Later changes to the original and the recipient's copy are not visible in each other's conversations.
claims.quote: Updates from the original sharer don't appear in your copy. Your changes don't appear in the original conversation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope: Recipients
claims.claim: Anyone in the organisation with a work or school sharing link can open it by signing in with their work or school account.
claims.quote: Work or school account: Anyone in your organization who has the link can open it by signing in with their work or school account.

claims.claim: MC1461700 says messages added after sharing remain private and are not included in the shared session.
claims.quote: Messages added after sharing remain private and are not included in the shared session.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Sharing does not give recipients access to referenced files, emails, chats, meetings or other Microsoft 365 content.
claims.quote: Sharing a Copilot session or response doesn't give recipients access to files, emails, chats, meetings, or other Microsoft 365 content referenced in the conversation.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 permissions govern recipients' ability to open referenced content.
claims.quote: People can open referenced files, emails, meetings, or chats only if they already have permission to access them.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; rationales
claims.claim: Sharing is on by default without administrator action.
claims.quote: Copilot sharing is turned on by default.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The sharing switch applies tenant-wide and cannot be scoped to specific users, groups or Entra ID groups.
claims.quote: An administrative control is available to enable or disable the feature across the tenant. The control cannot be scoped through Entra ID groups or other user/group-based targeting.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The switch is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > Copilot sharing > Allow users to share Copilot responses > Save.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, expand Copilot, and then select Settings. Select Copilot sharing. Select or clear Allow users to share Copilot responses. Select Save.

claims.claim: No API or automation for the sharing switch is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot sharing Graph PowerShell; Allow users to share Copilot responses API Graph PowerShell. Opened manage-content-sharing and copilotPolicySetting reference: UI steps only; supported Graph IDs contain no sharing setting.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope: Roles; Governance guidance
claims.claim: AI Reader can view the sharing settings.
claims.quote: View sharing settings: AI Reader

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope: Roles; Governance guidance
claims.claim: AI Admin can edit the sharing settings.
claims.quote: Edit sharing settings: AI Admin

claims.claim: Managing the setting requires access to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To access and manage Copilot sharing settings, you need access to the Microsoft 365 admin center and one of the following administrator roles:

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The switch also controls sharing of content with lower-sensitivity labels such as General or Public, or no sensitivity label.
claims.quote: This setting also controls whether users can share content with lower-sensitivity labels, such as General or Public, or no sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Sharing policies or sensitivity label protections can make some conversations or responses unavailable to share.
claims.quote: Some conversations or responses might not be available to share because of your organization's sharing policies or sensitivity label protections.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's sharing documentation does not identify which policies and labels block sharing or their interaction with the tenant switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot response sharing sensitivity policy. Opened sharing admin and user pages; read Purview DLP search passages. Sharing pages name no blocking labels; DLP passages concern grounding and prompt processing, not shared-link restrictions.

claims.claim: For personal-account links, anyone the link is shared with can open it by signing in with their Microsoft account.
claims.quote: Personal Microsoft account: Anyone you share the link with can open it by signing in with their Microsoft account.

claims.claim: Recipients must sign in before viewing shared content.
claims.quote: In either case, recipients must sign in before they can view the shared content.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anyone opening the link can read its included prompts and responses, including source text already quoted in those responses.
claims.quote: You see the conversation or response exactly as it appeared when it was shared. You can review the included prompts and responses.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can stop sharing links in Copilot > Settings > Data controls > Shared links.
claims.quote: Open Copilot. Go to Settings. Select Data controls. Select Shared links, where you can: ... Stop sharing an existing link. To stop sharing a link, find the link you want to remove and select Stop sharing.

claims.claim: Deleting the original conversation stops its sharing links from working.
claims.quote: If you delete the original conversation, any sharing links for that conversation also stop working.

claims.claim: The documented sharing experience is user-initiated, with no automatic sharing documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot session sharing automatic. Opened sharing admin and user pages: users select Share or Share response and Copy link. No automatic session or response link sharing described; unrelated Cowork scheduling results do not describe this feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning sharing off prevents new links and removes Share, including from the More options menu for a meeting.
claims.quote: Users can't create new session or response sharing links. The Share option doesn't appear in Copilot or Microsoft 365 apps, including the More options menu for a meeting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Changed settings apply to new sharing attempts after Save.
claims.quote: New settings apply to new sharing attempts after you select Save.

claims.claim: Existing recipient copies are unaffected by sharing setting changes.
claims.quote: Changes apply to new sharing attempts after you save the settings. Existing recipient copies aren't affected.

claims.claim: Administrators should allow time for settings changes to take effect.
claims.quote: Allow some time for a settings change to take effect across your organization.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing specific to this sharing feature is not published, so the feature's licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot sharing license session. Opened sharing admin/user pages, Microsoft Copilot requirements, license options and pay-as-you-go overview. Product licence requirements are stated; no distinct session/response sharing licensing terms are stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The sharing page's prerequisites name administrator roles and admin center access, but no licence.
claims.quote: To access and manage Copilot sharing settings, you need access to the Microsoft 365 admin center and one of the following administrator roles: View sharing settings: AI Reader; Edit sharing settings: AI Admin

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No Copilot Credits or other sharing-specific meter is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot sharing Copilot Credits; Copilot session response sharing license billing Copilot Credits. Opened sharing admin/user pages, requirements, license options and pay-as-you-go overview; no sharing-specific meter stated.

claims.claim: MC1461700 does not mention a charge.
claims.quote: No action is required if you want users in your organization to use this feature.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot requirements page documents general licence requirements but does not mention sharing.
claims.quote: Users need a Microsoft Copilot license and a qualifying prerequisite license.

claims.claim: The settings apply in the Microsoft Copilot app and Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.quote: These settings apply to Copilot sharing in the Microsoft Copilot app and Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: impact

claims.quote: Who is affected - All Microsoft 365 Copilot users.

claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: MC1461700 uses Copilot session and response sharing and Allow users to share Copilot sessions and responses, unlike Learn's shorter labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > Copilot session and response sharing - Clear the Allow users to share Copilot sessions and responses setting.

claims.claim: The copilotPolicySetting reference lists five supported settings and none is sharing.
claims.quote: Pin Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat; Block Copilot Access to Open Content; Control access to Designer Image Generation; Allow web search in Copilot; Control Admin Copilot availability in Microsoft 365 Admin Center

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview records sharing events, link access and blocked sharing attempts.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview records Copilot sharing activity, including sharing events, link access, and blocked sharing attempts.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The sharing management page gives neither audit operation names nor an audit portal path.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot sharing audit operation. Opened sharing management page in full: activity descriptions and a Security Copilot audit link, but no operation names or portal steps. General Copilot audit search results give a portal path, not sharing operation names.

claims.claim: The tenant-wide sharing switch is the only documented administrator control specifically for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot session sharing groups; Copilot sharing Graph PowerShell; Copilot response sharing sensitivity policy. Opened sharing admin/user pages and copilotPolicySetting reference: one primary switch; no additional feature-specific admin control found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, At rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The checklist names sensitivity label review, user shared-link management and Purview audit review without corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'ask whether your sensitivity label setup is relevant'; 'Shared links lets them stop sharing a link'; 'Review Microsoft Purview audit records'. Table: tenant sharing switch and user/group scoping only.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Check which teams handle material', remove the After rollout audit-review bullet, and remove ', and that Copilot > Settings > Data controls > Shared links lets them stop sharing a link' from the At rollout communication bullet. The verified explanatory body can remain.

claims.claim: The briefing calls the product Microsoft 365 Copilot, its former name.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot is now named Microsoft Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is now named Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.fix: Use 'Microsoft Copilot' in the title and unattributed running prose. Retain the original product name when reporting the roadmap record or quoting MC1461700.
